[Discussion] For anyone who watches others play on the Internet: do you prefer live streams or non-live stream let's plays?

I don't watch a ton of them in general, but if I do, it's probably because I'm thinking about buying a game and want to see it in action. That means I'd want to have the ability to skip time around to get a good sample, so non-live.
not live, and edited. especially if it is a single player game and i am watching to see the game. in that case i want them to edit out any times they died and had to repeat part of the game.
Worst is the combination of post-live stream watching. It's like someone's talking to a telephone.
Depends on the game, whether it's a letsplay or a speedrun, and the person playing it. Usually, I prefer non-live stream, but I like live streaming speedruns more.

I prefer videos because the video is made without the distraction of a live audience.

I've just seen too many live streams where the streamer is 10 minutes into the stream and all of a sudden it's snack time and I have to listen to them chew for the next 20 minutes.

Or streamers who already have a highly profitable Youtube channel and whose streams are almost about donations with gameplay in the background for every time they say the word "donation". I almost want to take a recording of the guy standing on the corner outside the drug store and see if he says "spare change" more or less often than some streamers say "donation". A lot of streamers come across like the first panhandlers on the internet and it drives me bonkers. A busker playing an instrument with a case in front of them gathering tips doesn't stop playing every time someone tosses in a quarter to point at them and say, "Hey look everyone! That guy just gave me a quarter."

It's important for a streamer to interact with their audience, but if someone says, "Hey, I'm streaming <x> game at <time>!" then I expect the stream to be about the game, not yammering at the chat box for 10 minutes at a time. Chat with the audience during loading screens ot cutscenes when there's a natural pause in the action. When you pick one comment to chat about you run the risk of alienating the rest of your audience in the process because they tuned in to watch you plane <x> game, not babble about Derek Smart. If you say you're streaming DOTA2 for 2-3 hours and 90% of your stream is you playing DOTA2, nobody can complain that they didn't get what they were offered. When you say you're going to stream DOTA2 for 2-3 hours and 30% of the time is streaming DOTA2 and the rest of the time is divided between donations talk, random conversations with people posting comments, and opening another bag of obscure snack foods that you bought from the local ehtnic market, I'll never watch you stream again.

Thus ends the first draft of my "how not to be a shit streamer" manifesto.

My thoughts exactly. I prefer watching well edited videos with some thought put into them. Livestreams can be really boring and full of irrelevant shit.
